extracted.intended_audience: attorneys who practice before the USPTO (trademark and other non-patent matters), OED/disciplinary counsel, and law firms advising such practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements governing attorney conduct before the USPTO in trademark and non‑patent matters, including conflict-of-interest rules, client communication duties, third‑party payment rules, and the sanctions/process for disciplinary violations. The page is a Final Order approving a settlement and sets out violated rules and required sanctions/compliance steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO disciplinary jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners who practice before the Office in trademark matters are subject to the disciplinary jurisdiction of the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. § 11.19; the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility (37 C.F.R. §§ 10.20–10.112); and the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.101–11.901).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director has jurisdiction pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.19. Disciplinary proceedings and sanctions (e.g., suspension, probation) are imposed under these authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.62(a) — consent after full disclosure when practitioner's judgment may be affected
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to obtain consent after full disclosure from a client to accept employment if the exercise of the practitioner's professional judgment on behalf of the client will be, or reasonably may be, affected by the practitioner's own financial, business, property, or personal interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent admitted violating this provision by jointly representing co-owners while having other clients with potentially conflicting interests and by not disclosing risks or obtaining consent after full disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.66(a)–(c) — declining or avoiding proffered employment with differing interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to decline proffered employment if the exercise of the practitioner's independent professional judgment on behalf of a client will be adversely affected or would involve the practitioner in representing differing interests; continuing employment of multiple clients when independent judgment is likely to be adversely affected or would involve representing differing interests without obtaining consent after full disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicable where a practitioner represents multiple clients (e.g., joint owners) and also represents other related parties, creating an irreconcilable conflict (as found between Client 1 and Client 6).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.68(a)(1)–(2) and (b) — accepting third‑party compensation or value without consent; third‑party direction
rubrics_metrics.description: Without obtaining consent after full disclosure from the client, accepting compensation from one other than the practitioner's client for the practitioner's legal services; accepting from one other than the client's anything of value related to representation; allowing a person who pays the practitioner to render legal services for another to direct the practitioner's professional judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent billed time to a third party (Client 5) for work for Clients 1 and 2 and did not disclose or obtain consent. The rule prohibits accepting such third‑party payment or allowing payor direction absent informed consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to conduct conflict checks before undertaking representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Before undertaking representation practitioners must check for conflicts of interest to determine whether representing new clients will conflict with existing clients and must take appropriate steps (decline, obtain informed consent, or otherwise manage conflict).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stipulated fact: Respondent did not conduct a conflict check prior to undertaking representation of Client 1 and Client 2 while representing Clients 3–5, which the Order treats as a failure to meet ethical obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to disclose third‑party payment and obtain informed consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must disclose to clients when a third party is paying the client's legal fees and must obtain the client's informed consent (and not accept direction from the payor that would compromise the client's interests).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent did not disclose that Client 5 was paying Client 1 and Client 2's fees, did not disclose limits on direction from the third party, and failed to obtain consent after full disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.102(a) — consult and abide by client's objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to abide by a client's decisions concerning the objectives of representation and failing to consult with the client as to the means by which the objectives are pursued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites Respondent's failure to consult with Client 1 about the Express Abandonment and other strategic decisions as a violation of this duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(1)–(2) and (b) — inform and explain matters sufficiently for informed consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to promptly inform the client of any decision or circumstance with respect to which the client's informed consent is required; failing to consult with the client about means by which the client's objectives are to be accomplished; failing to explain a matter to the extent reasonably necessary to permit the client to make informed decisions regarding the representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent failed to inform Client 1 of communications and decisions (e.g., abandonment filing) and failed to allow a reasonable opportunity to object, demonstrating breach of these duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.107(a)(1)–(2) and (b)(3)–(4) — representing clients with directly adverse or materially limited interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Representing a client when that representation will be directly adverse to another client, or when the representation may be materially limited by the lawyer's responsibilities to another client; representing a client asserting a claim against another represented client in the same proceeding without obtaining consent after full disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order finds an irreconcilable conflict between Client 1 and Client 6 (Client 6's applications were filed for the same mark after abandonment), and Respondent both filed abandonment and later filed a Petition to reinstate that would be adverse to Client 6's applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.108(f)(1)–(3) — third‑party compensation and interference with independence/confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Representing a client and accepting compensation for representing that client from one other than the client unless the client gives informed consent; accepting compensation when there is interference with the practitioner's independence or with the client-practitioner relationship; accepting compensation and failing to protect information relating to representation as required under confidentiality rule 37 C.F.R. § 11.106.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent accepted billing to Client 5 while representing Clients 1 and 2, did not obtain consent, and failed to protect client communications (e.g., excluding Client 1 from communications), which the Order treats as violative.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.109(a) — representing a former client adverse to a current client without written informed consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Representing a former client and thereafter representing another client in the same or substantially related matter in which the interests of that new client are materially adverse to the interests of the former client without obtaining informed consent, confirmed in writing, from the former client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited where representation of related parties over time creates potential adverse positions without written informed consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.504(c) — prohibiting payor direction or regulation of practitioner judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowing a person who pays the practitioner to render legal services to another to direct or regulate the practitioner's professional judgment in rendering such legal services is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The facts (third‑party paying and directing filings/exclusions of Client 1) illustrate the misconduct this rule forbids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to reasonably consult with and give clients meaningful time to object to significant filings (e.g., Express Abandonment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before filing actions that materially affect a client's ownership or rights (such as an Express Abandonment of a co-owned trademark application), a practitioner must consult and give the client a reasonable and meaningful opportunity to state objections or take action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent filed an Express Abandonment of the co-owned application without consulting Client 1 or giving a reasonable time to object; the Order treats that as a procedural/ethical lapse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction — thirty (30) day suspension from practice before the Office in trademark and other non‑patent matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from practice before the Office in trademark and other non‑patent matters for thirty (30) days, commencing fourteen (14) days after the Final Order is signed. During suspension the respondent shall not engage in trademark or other non‑patent law as defined by 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.5(b)(1) and 11.5(b)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension is a primary disciplinary sanction imposed here; limited recognition for thirty days under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(c) is not granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to pass the MPRE (within one year) with score ≥85 and provide declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Within one year of the date of the Final Order, Respondent shall take the Multi‑State Professional Responsibility Examination (MPRE), attain a score of 85 or better, and provide a declaration to the OED Director verifying compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an educational/competency requirement imposed as part of the sanction package.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thirteen (13) month probation with practice monitor
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall serve a thirteen (13) month probation commencing on the date of the Final Order and shall have an attorney in good standing and active status of any state bar serve as a practice monitor during the probation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The practice monitor must certify compliance with USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct and file four quarterly compliance reports with the OED Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice monitor reporting schedule and coverage periods
rubrics_metrics.description: The practice monitor must file four compliance reports: first at five months after the Final Order (covering the 90 days commencing one month after the Final Order), second at eight months (covering the 90 days commencing four months after), third at eleven months (covering the 90 days commencing seven months after), and fourth at fourteen months (covering the 90 days commencing ten months after).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each report must certify whether Respondent's practice before the Office complies with USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct; the schedule and coverage windows are set out in detail in the Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing Legal Education (CLE) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall attend specified CLE seminars concerning conflicts of interest and conflicts management (including a Massachusetts Board of Bar Overseers seminar in June 2015) and has already completed two CLEs on conflicts on March 16 and April 2, 2015.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order requires additional CLE attendance as mitigation and compliance measure; the Official Notice recites that Respondent agreed to take three CLE classes concerning conflicts and other ethical responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation with OED and reporting/publication requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall cooperate with the OED Director in any requests for information or testimony in disciplinary matters; the OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order in OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the notice provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication and cooperation are required parts of the disciplinary disposition and notice to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement and compliance with 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58 and 11.60 (with limited waivers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must comply with provisions governing suspension, notification, reinstatement petitions, and related fees under 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58 and 11.60, except where specific provisions are waived by the Agreement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.3(a). Respondent must file a petition for reinstatement with required attestations and fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order sets out numerous specific sub‑paragraphs requiring compliance (and lists waivers); reinstatement requires sworn declarations of compliance and filing the fee at 37 C.F.R. § 1.21(a)(10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for probationary noncompliance — Order to Show Cause and possible additional suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If during probation the OED Director believes Respondent failed to comply with the Final Order or Rules, the OED Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause, send it to Respondent, grant 15 days to respond, and may request that the USPTO Director enter an order immediately suspending Respondent for up to an additional twelve (12) months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order describes the procedures: issuance of Order to Show Cause, service to last address on record, a 15‑day response period, and forwarding materials to the USPTO Director for additional suspension if noncompliance persists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing prevents the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order, in addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct or in any future disciplinary proceeding as an aggravating factor or to rebut statements by Respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order can be used in future discipline or reconsideration matters and is expressly preserved for such purposes.
